C0.quote: eliciting agents’ preferences with the goal of finding a Kemeny ranking
C0.note: Elicitation for the Kemeny voting rule; computational and sample-complexity aspects of a voting procedure.

C1.quote: we formulate PAC algorithms for Kemeny rankings w.r.t. Kemeny scores
C1.note: PAC algorithms with sample complexity bounds are the bulk of the results; experiments on synthetic data are secondary.

C2.2.quote: linear orders v ∈ L(C) for v ∈ N
C2.2.note: Profile of linear orders; the rule is applied to a pairwise matrix of fractions of voters preferring i over j. Voters answer pairwise queries.

C2.3.note: Voters' preferences are referred to throughout.

C2.4.quote: preferences of the voters over the alternatives to be linear orders
C2.4.note: Preferences are taken as the input and the rule is applied directly. Nothing is said about reporting or truthfulness.

C3.2.note: No statement that voters answer truthfully.

C4.1.note: The paper mentions 'voter satisfaction' loosely, but there is no utility model for voters. Kemeny score is a disagreement measure. Treated as not applicable.

C5.1.note: Outcomes are evaluated by Kemeny score, a voter-disagreement measure. This is arguably a representation or satisfaction criterion.

C5.2.quote: the matrices in the proofs also yield similar voter satisfaction
C5.2.note: Kemeny score is evaluated on the preference matrix, with no statement relating it to held attitudes.

VOT.note: Voters are randomly sampled and answer queries as fixed data. They take no action in the model.

ORG.note: The elicitor chooses which pairs to query (adaptive sampling), which could count as an organiser. Judged here as the algorithm itself rather than an agent.

This can be excessively time consuming or costly for voters

C9.1.note: Motivational claims about fairness and voter cost in the introduction. The conclusion makes no such claims.

C9.2.note: The claim about a good societal outcome via fair aggregation would need an assumption that elicited answers reflect voters' true preferences. This is not stated.
